title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Seriously Studying and Implementing the Anti-Monopoly Law of the People's Republic of China
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Earnestly Studying and Implementing the Anti-Monopoly Law of the People's Republic of China

Fa Fa [2008] No. 23

To: the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Anti-Monopoly Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Anti-Monopoly Law) was adopted at the 29th Session of the Standing Committee of the Tenth National People's Congress on August 30, 2007, and will come into force on August 1, 2008. In order to correctly apply the Anti-Monopoly Law and properly adjudicate cases related to the Anti-Monopoly Law, the relevant issues concerning the study and implementation of the Anti-Monopoly Law are hereby notified as follows:

1. Fully recognize the significant importance of implementing the Anti-Monopoly Law

The Anti-Monopoly Law is a fundamental law for curbing monopolistic conduct, protecting market competition, and maintaining market order. It is also an important law for improving market structure, ensuring economic security, and securing the fundamental role of the market in allocating resources. The Anti-Monopoly Law plays an extremely important role in safeguarding the lawful rights and interests of business operators and consumers, promoting technological innovation and progress, enhancing the competitiveness of enterprises, and ensuring the healthy, sustained, and coordinated development of the national economy. People's courts at all levels shall earnestly study and implement the Anti-Monopoly Law, correctly comprehend the legislative intent of the Anti-Monopoly Law, give full play to the function of trial work, and, by lawfully adjudicating anti-monopoly cases, curb illegal monopolistic conduct, protect the lawful rights and interests of business operators and consumers, and maintain a fair competitive market order.

2. Lawfully adjudicate all types of anti-monopoly cases

Article 50 of the Anti-Monopoly Law provides: "Where a business operator engages in monopolistic conduct and causes losses to others, it shall bear civil liability in accordance with the law." Where a party initiates a civil lawsuit due to monopolistic conduct, if it meets the acceptance conditions stipulated in Article 108 of the Civil Procedure Law and the Anti-Monopoly Law, the People's Court shall accept the case in accordance with the law and adjudicate it in accordance with the law. The Anti-Monopoly Law is closely related to curbing the abuse of intellectual property rights and protecting intellectual property rights, and together with the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, falls within the category of competition law. The "Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Causes of Action in Civil Cases," which came into effect on April 1 of this year, collectively stipulates monopoly disputes and various unfair competition disputes, uniformly incorporating them into the scope of intellectual property disputes. Accordingly, the trial divisions responsible for the trial of intellectual property cases in People's Courts at all levels shall perform their trial duties in accordance with the law and properly adjudicate anti-monopoly civil cases involving the abuse of intellectual property rights, as well as all other types of anti-monopoly civil cases.

Where a citizen, legal person, or other organization is dissatisfied with a specific administrative act made by an anti-monopoly enforcement agency pursuant to the Anti-Monopoly Law and initiates an administrative lawsuit, it shall be determined, in accordance with the Administrative Procedure Law and Article 53 of the Anti-Monopoly Law, whether administrative reconsideration is required. For cases that should be accepted by the People's Court, provided that they meet the conditions for filing a lawsuit as stipulated in the Administrative Procedure Law, the People's Court shall accept the case in accordance with the law and adjudicate it in accordance with the law.

3. Strengthen investigation and research work, and conscientiously summarize the experience of anti-monopoly trials

Anti-monopoly cases are highly difficult and complex, with economic and legal issues interwoven. They are highly specialized, have a significant impact on enterprises and industries, and some cases even involve the economic security of the country. Some provisions of the Anti-Monopoly Law are relatively principled and abstract, and the operational provisions involving People's Courts are relatively simple. Therefore, many new situations and problems will be encountered in the trial of anti-monopoly cases. People's Courts at all levels should take precautions, make early arrangements and responses, earnestly conduct investigation and research, and timely summarize trial experience. In particular, research should be strengthened on issues such as case jurisdiction, plaintiff qualification, proper defendant, determination of monopolistic conduct, assumption of civil liability, and the standards for the legality of specific administrative acts under the Anti-Monopoly Law. New situations, new problems encountered in the application of the Anti-Monopoly Law, and research findings shall be promptly reported level by level to the Supreme People's Court. For major anti-monopoly cases, the system of reporting major and important cases level by level shall be earnestly implemented.

All the above items shall be observed.

July 28, 2008
